newsitem.title: UK: Conoco, BP to develop more Viking gas in UK N. Sea.
newsitem.headline: Conoco, BP to develop more Viking gas in UK N. Sea.

text.p: Conoco (UK) Ltd, operator of the North Sea's Viking gas fields, and co-venturer BP, have received consent from the UK's Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) to develop further reserves, Conoco said on Wednesday.

The four reserves are F/Fs, part of the Viking A field, and Gn/Wx, part of the Viking E field. They are located in blocks 49/12a and 49/17, around 100 km east of the Lincolnshire coast in the southern sector of the North Sea.
The four new areas contain recoverable reserves of approximately 500 billion cubic feet of gas. First production is expected in the fourth quarter of 1998.

Development will be carried out by two platforms which will normally be unmanned. Gas from all four reserves will be transported through the existing Viking Transport System (VTS) to the Conoco-operated Theddlethorpe terminal in Lincolnshire.
The first Viking field, Viking A, came onstream on October 1 1972. Since then, the Viking fields have produced over 2.8 trillion cubic feet of gas.
